instruction:
Open /home/user/Desktop/rest_shape.step in FreeCAD 0.21.2 Path/CAM. To use FreeCAD, run `freecad` from a terminal (use the full executable path if it is not on PATH). At the start of the task, use `/usr/lib/freecad/bin/freecadcmd-python3` for FreeCAD Path command-line automation when working on `rest_shape.step`.

The model is a 120 x 80 x 18 mm part with a nominal cross-shaped pocket floor at absolute model Z=6.000 mm. The cross consists of a central 60 x 36 mm region (X=-30..30, Y=-18..18) and four narrow residual regions: X=-4..4, Y=18..30; X=-4..4, Y=-30..-18; X=-42..-30, Y=-4..4; and X=30..42, Y=-4..4. Create one native Path Job using the source model and stock equal to its 120 x 80 x 18 mm bounding box, with exactly two native operations in this order. First use a native Pocket Shape operation with native T1 of 10 mm cutting diameter on the central region. Then, because FreeCAD 0.21.2 has no native Rest Machining operation or automatic previous-operation rest-stock linkage, implement the version-correct equivalent with a native Adaptive operation in Clearing mode using native T2 of 4 mm cutting diameter on the four explicit narrow residual boundaries. The nominal selected regions have the stated planar extents; the cutter sweep may naturally leave cutter-radius internal corners. Both operations must start at Z=18.000 mm, finish at Z=6.000 mm, leave no stock, use S7000 rpm, and use F500 mm/min for both horizontal and vertical cutting feeds. Use exactly G54, the LinuxCNC postprocessor, and millimeters; do not override the LinuxCNC preamble or postamble. Save the editable document and its directly posted program using exactly these absolute file paths: /home/user/Desktop/task-08.FCStd and /home/user/Desktop/task-08.nc.
